title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master on Coordinated Humanitarian Response, Health and Displacement (Human Response) 2027-2029
organization: Human Response consortium, coordinated by Iscte - University Institute of Lisbon (with NTNU Norway, Makerere University Uganda, and partners in Cape Verde, Greece and Mozambique)
overview: Two-year, 120 ECTS Erasmus Mundus joint master in humanitarian action taught in English, with semesters in Portugal (Iscte), Norway (NTNU) and Uganda (Makerere), a summer school and a fourth-semester dissertation with one of 23 associated partners. Courses include management, project management, logistics, public health and evaluation in humanitarian action. 15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships per edition.
country: Portugal, Norway, Uganda (plus dissertation fieldwork abroad)
program_dates: 2027-2029 edition, two years (120 ECTS). Semester 1 at Iscte (Portugal), semester 2 at NTNU (Norway), mandatory two-week summer school (the programme page lists Uganda for intake 3, June 2028), semester 3 at Makerere (Uganda) with an internship, semester 4 dissertation. Exact start date not stated on the pages read.
deadline_text: Applications page: 'Scholarship Applications for the 2027/2029 edition OPEN' and 'Scholarship round of Applications end 7 January 2027'. No time is given.
deadline_timezone: Not stated (coordinating university in Lisbon, Portugal)
funding_details: 'Student scholarships are allocated as per the Erasmus Mundus guidelines for 15 scholarships per edition.'
'Each student will be allocated 1400 Euros per month.' Payments start 'only after their arrival for the beginning of activities'.
'Students with scholarship do not pay fees.'
'24 months insurance is provided to all students.'

The page lists travel between the mobility countries, housing, living expenses and visa/residence permit costs as 'Typical costs (every students)', so they are paid out of the monthly allowance rather than covered separately
Self-funded route: 'Tuition fee is 16.000,00 EUR for the two years of the Master'
'Erasmus Mundus Human Response applicants do not need to pay application fees.'
Students who already held an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship are not eligible for another
participation_fee: No application fee ('Erasmus Mundus Human Response applicants do not need to pay application fees')
stipend: EUR 1,400 per month (scholarship holders), paid from arrival
eligibility: 'Only candidates with a Bachelor degree (180 ECTS) can be admitted.'

'Proof of English proficiency is mandatory': TOEFL iBT 92, IELTS Academic 6.5 (no band below 5.5), PTE Academic 76, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180, or Duolingo 135 (no component below 100); tests valid if taken up to 2 years and 5 months before applying

Exemption from the English test if the whole bachelor's programme was taught in English (stated on the diploma/transcript or in a registrar's letter), or for certain English-medium secondary education

Selection weights: level of academic qualification 30%, relevance of academic qualification 15%, research experience 5%, professional experience 20%, statement of purpose 20%, fit with programme goals and cohort 10%
nationality_requirements: No nationality restriction stated on the applications page; the programme says it focuses on 'students, professionals and academics from affected countries' and on delivering education in Africa
education_requirement: Bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS; fields not restricted on the page read (relevance of the degree is scored at 15%)
experience_requirement: No minimum stated; relevance and level of professional experience count for 20% of the score
language_requirement: English test at the levels listed (TOEFL iBT 92 / IELTS 6.5 / PTE 76 / Cambridge 180 / Duolingo 135), unless exempt
other_requirements: Two signed and dated recommendation letters
documents_required: English test certificate with validation code
application_process: Read the mandatory information on the applications page
Apply through the 'APPLY HERE' link on the applications page before 7 January 2027
Upload all mandatory documents; incomplete applications are not considered
Candidates may be called to an interview to attest English level
eligibility_reason: The Licence meets the degree rule if it is recognised as 180 ECTS, and no nationality or field restriction is stated. The profile records no English test score, which is mandatory unless the Licence was taught entirely in English.
potential_issues: An English test certificate (e.g. IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 135) is needed before 7 January 2027 unless an exemption applies
Travel, housing and visa costs for Portugal, Norway and Uganda come out of the EUR 1,400 monthly allowance, and payments start only after arrival, so the first flight and visa must be paid upfront
Schengen visas for Portugal and Norway would be needed
Professional experience counts for 20% of the score and the profile has under one year
benefits: Tuition waived and EUR 1,400 per month for scholarship holders
Courses in management, project management, logistics and evaluation in humanitarian action
Study in three countries, including a semester and internship in Uganda
Dissertation fieldwork with one of 23 associated partners (NGOs, ministries, universities)
relevance_reason: The programme targets candidates from crisis-affected countries and trains managers of humanitarian programmes, matching the profile's logistics, programme-coordination and vaccination-campaign monitoring experience. Access depends mainly on getting an English test score in time.

visa.required: Yes (Portugal and Norway; Uganda for semester 3)

upfront_cost_risk: English test fee; first flight and visa costs before the allowance starts on arrival
action: Book an accepted English test now (Duolingo or IELTS) so the result arrives before 7 January 2027, then apply through humanresponse.eu with the statement of purpose and two recommendation letters.
notes: Programme listed in the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue as 'Coordinated Humanitarian Response, Health and Displacement'. The home page states '7 universities (3 from Europe and 4 from Africa)' and '100 vacancies in 4 editions'. The applications page gives the summer-school intake date as '3 june 2028' for this edition.
match_keywords: coordinated humanitarian response, health and displacement

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Greening Energy Market and Finance (GrEnFIn) 2027-2029
organization: University of Bologna (coordinator), Ludwig-Maximilian University Munich and Université Paris-Dauphine
overview: Two-year, 120 ECTS Erasmus Mundus joint master on the low-carbon energy transition with three tracks: Renewable Technologies, Environmental Finance, and Energy-Climate Economics for the Business Sector (Climate&Business). Students study in Italy, Germany and France and receive three degrees. Up to 18 Erasmus Mundus scholarships for 2027-28.
city: Bologna; Munich; Paris (Renewable Technologies track starts at Dauphine's London campus)
program_dates: Programme start 6 September 2027 (welcome week at UNIBO 31 August - 3 September 2027); 24 months.
deadline_text: Admission notice A.Y. 2027/2028, section 2.1: 'Opening of applications ... October 14, 2026 - h 11:00 am CET'; 'Closing date for applications ... January 7, 2027 - h 11:00 am CET'. Results (admission and scholarship) 26 February 2027; acceptance 1-5 March 2027.
funding_details: 'a maximum of 18 full Erasmus Mundus scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide' for 2027-2028
The scholarship 'shall cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs. It is calculated on the basis of a monthly unit cost of € 1.400' for the whole study period
Only non-scholarship holders pay 'student participation costs' at enrolment; scholarship holders complete matriculation steps 1 and 2 only
No more than 10% of scholarships to candidates of the same nationality
'All applicants, wherever they come from, are eligible for an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship provided they fulfil the academic requirements'
No application fee is mentioned in the admission notice
participation_fee: Not mentioned in the admission notice
eligibility: First-cycle degree (three-year university degree) or a recognised foreign qualification; final-year students may apply if they graduate by 23 July 2027

Curricular requirement: 'a Bachelor's degree in one of the following fields: Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Statistical Sciences, Information Technology, Engineering' (the equivalent Italian classes include L-18 Business Administration)

'English language skills are required to at least CEFR level B2', proved by a recognised certificate (online tests accepted); exempt only for nationals or graduates of the USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland or UK
Assessment: academic merit up to 60 points, overall experience (Europass CV) up to 30, optional GRE/GMAT up to 10; minimum 60 points; 80 or more leads to an interview that decides the scholarship
nationality_requirements: Open to EU and non-EU candidates; 'All applicants, wherever they come from, are eligible' for the scholarship if they meet the academic requirements
education_requirement: Bachelor's in Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Statistical Sciences, Information Technology or Engineering (Business Administration is listed among the equivalent Italian degree classes)
experience_requirement: None required; curricular and extracurricular experience scored up to 30 points
other_requirements: Interview (preferably in person in Bologna, Munich or Paris, online for justified reasons) for candidates scoring 80 or more
documents_required: Degree certificate and transcript translated into English
application_process: Register on Studenti Online (studenti.unibo.it) as an international student
Choose 'Admission application' > Second Cycle Degree Programme and one GrEnFIn track
Upload the documents and accept the Erasmus Mundus scholarship conditions before 7 January 2027, 11:00 CET
eligibility_reason: The curricular rule for foreign degrees lists Economics but not Business Administration (which appears only among the equivalent Italian classes), so the board must accept the Licence as equivalent. The profile also records no English B2 certificate.
potential_issues: Business Administration is not named in the field list for foreign degrees; acceptance is up to the Admission Board
Quantitative programme (finance, statistics, energy economics); a weak maths background lowers the academic-merit score
English B2 certificate needed before 7 January 2027
Only 18 scholarships across three tracks; flights and visas are paid from the monthly allowance
The programme's application page (greening-energy-market-finance-emjm.eu/application) returned HTTP 403 to the reader, so the list of accepted English certificates was not read
benefits: Climate&Business track aimed at the business sector
Study in Italy, Germany and France
relevance_reason: A funded master's in energy markets and finance with a business track, but the field rule favours economics and quantitative degrees, so a business Licence is a borderline fit.

visa.support: Admitted students are informed about visa or residence-permit requirements for their track

upfront_cost_risk: English test fee; translation of diploma and transcript
action: Ask the programme (via the contacts in the admission notice) whether a Licence in Business Administration meets the curricular requirement before investing in an application; if yes, apply on Studenti Online before 7 January 2027, 11:00 CET, choosing the Climate&Business track.
notes: Online information session announced on the programme site for 27 October 2026, 09:00-11:00 CEST. The programme site header calls it 'edition 2027-2029' while the notice is for A.Y. 2027/2028. A maximum of 51 places for 2027-28.

title: Schwarzman Scholars (Class of 2028-2029)
overview: One-year master's programme in global affairs at Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University, Beijing, described by the organiser as 'fully funded'. Open to applicants from any country aged 18 to 28 with an undergraduate degree.
deadline_text: Admissions page: U.S./Global applicants 'Application period: Apr 2027 - Sep 2027'; selection cycle Oct - Nov 2027; programme begins Aug 2028. Application instructions: 'The U.S. and Global application for the class of 2028-2029 will be open from April 2027 to September 2027.' The class of 2027-2028 window is closed. No exact closing day is given yet.
expected_next_cycle: Class of 2028-2029: Global application open April 2027 to September 2027 (official admissions page); interviews late October (London) and early November (New York). Exact deadline not yet published.
funding_details: Home page: 'fully funded master's program in global affairs at Tsinghua University'

FAQ: the scholarship covers tuition, fees, room and board, travel to and from Beijing at the start and end of the year, in-country study tours, required course books and supplies, a laptop, health insurance and a personal stipend
FAQ: 'There is no fee associated with applying to the program.'
participation_fee: None ('There is no fee associated with applying to the program')
eligibility: 'Must have an undergraduate degree' (completed before 1 August 2028)
'Candidates must be at least 18 but not yet 29 years of age as of August 1 of their Schwarzman Scholars enrollment year' (1 August 2028)
English proficiency: native speaker, two years in an English-language degree programme, or a test score (TOEFL iBT 100, IELTS 7, Duolingo 130, Cambridge C1/C2 185)
U.S./Global applicants must be non-Chinese citizens holding a regular passport from a country other than China
Selection on leadership, character and integrity, academic ability, empathy and intercultural competency, open-mindedness and entrepreneurial spirit
nationality_requirements: Any nationality other than Chinese for the Global application; the FAQ states class targets of 40% U.S., 20% China, 40% rest of the world
age_requirement: At least 18 and not yet 29 on 1 August 2028
experience_requirement: No minimum stated (the application has space for up to two full-time positions)
language_requirement: English: TOEFL iBT 100, IELTS 7, Duolingo 130 or Cambridge 185, unless waived through English-medium study
other_requirements: Three recommenders registered in the online system
documents_required: Leadership essay (750 words) and statement of purpose (500 words)
application_process: Apply online during the Global window (April to September 2027)
Interview invitations mid-October; in-person interviews in London (late October) or New York (early November)
eligibility_reason: The degree and nationality rules are met. The profile records only 'under 30', not whether the applicant will still be under 29 on 1 August 2028, and it records no English test score (TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7 / Duolingo 130 are required unless waived).
potential_issues: Interviews are in person in London or New York; the pages read do not say whether interview travel is paid
Chinese student visa needed; visa costs not mentioned
Exact closing date for the 2027 window not yet published
benefits: Full scholarship including flights to and from Beijing, room and board, insurance and a stipend
Master's degree from Tsinghua University in one year
relevance_reason: A fully funded, open-nationality master's with no stated experience minimum; it rewards demonstrated leadership more than field of study. The age limit on 1 August 2028 and the English threshold are the deciding constraints.
upfront_cost_risk: English test fee; possible travel to an in-person interview
action: Check that the age will still be under 29 on 1 August 2028; if so, take an English test (IELTS 7 or Duolingo 130 target) and line up three recommenders before the window opens in April 2027.
notes: The 2027-2028 class window is closed. The FAQ describes the annual pattern for non-Chinese applicants as 'April to September'.
